title: Six simulated velocity visits separate tested HD 303514 eclipse-loss and survival states after yearly offsets and free amplitude
abstract: We calculate a velocity test of five fixed HD 303514 states that give different primary eclipse forecasts. Three lose overlap and two retain it. We integrate their Newtonian states and search monthly date grids. With six visits in 2027-2028, a fitted amplitude and separate yearly velocity constants leave a minimum cross-class shape distance of 0.02714 times the component velocity half-range K. Independent equal errors of 0.00543 K give expected model distance 5. This is 0.179 km/s at K = 33 km/s. The best one-season six-visit test has 36.8 times less distance. Seven-day date-shift corner tests retain 0.02424 K. An added linear velocity trend reduces the selected design distance to 0.01387 K. A two-visit test is exactly degenerate under free offset and amplitude. Numerical and independent projection checks pass. These are tests of fixed examples, not full orbit families, detection probabilities or new observations. A measurable tertiary line or a recovered pair centre-of-mass velocity is required. Line blending, source fit assumptions and orbit refitting limit the result. Code, states, simulated curves and a complete offline reproduction route are included.
